mainTopic: Whether knowing about a doubt between sins (ידיעות ספק) splits them into separate חטאות and אשמות תלויים
overview: The amud begins by finishing an earlier case. According to רבי אליעזר, a person may bring an אשם תלוי as a volunteer offering, so he can bring one with a condition attached. Then a ברייתא asks about someone who twice ate fat that might have been חלב and was told of the doubt each time. רבי says he brings an אשם תלוי for each time; other תנאים say only one. רבי זירא learns from רבי that knowing about a doubt also splits the sins into separate חטאות. רבא disagrees, and אביי defends רבי זירא's rule. רבא בר חנן, רב אידי בר אבין and רבא challenge אביי from cases where יום הכפורים, which atones like an אשם תלוי, falls between two sins, and each challenge gets an answer. ריש לקיש agrees with רבי זירא and רבי יוחנן agrees with רבא. The ברייתא's wording is left as a קשיא against ריש לקיש. Finally the גמרא begins to show that each of them seems to contradict himself, using a ברייתא about two paths, one impure and one pure.

steps.title: The case follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the case just discussed follows רבי אליעזר. He holds that a person may bring an אשם תלוי as a volunteer offering every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי אליעזר, who says a person may volunteer to bring an אשם תלוי every day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question from just before this section. It says the case works only according to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an אשם תלוי is brought only by someone who really might have sinned. רבי אליעזר holds that a person may bring one on his own, even with no specific doubt. That opinion lets someone bring this offering even when he may not need it.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'provisional' guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he committed a sin that would require a חטאת
Volunteers; brings something on his own without being obligated

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the case in the previous lines can work at all, since it depends on bringing an אשם תלוי by choice.

phrases.english: It is the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer,
who says: a person may volunteer
a provisional guilt offering every day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from the text just before this section by naming whose opinion the case follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed hard to understand how someone could bring an אשם תלוי without a real obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אליעזר, an אשם תלוי may be brought as a volunteer offering on any day.

steps.title: Bring the offering with a condition
steps.stepSummary: Because of רבי אליעזר's view, the second person is told to bring an אשם תלוי with a condition. If he is the one who ate the חלב, it is his כפרה. If not, it is a נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we tell him: bring an אשם תלוי and stipulate. If the first person ate the permitted fat, then I ate the חלב, so let this be my atonement. If not, let it be a gift offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses רבי אליעזר's rule in practice. The second person brings the offering with a two-way condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one of the two people ate the חלב. The second person does not know whether he needs an atonement. The condition makes his offering correct either way: it is a כפרה if he sinned and a voluntary gift if he did not.

keyTerms.meaning: And make a stipulation (a condition)
Permitted fat
Forbidden fat
Atonement
A voluntary gift offering

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, an אשם תלוי can be brought with a condition: atonement if he sinned, a gift offering if he did not.

phrases.english: Therefore, we say to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the second person in the case from just before.

phrases.english: Bring a provisional guilt offering and stipulate:
If the first one ate the permitted fat,
then he ate the forbidden fat,
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the second person himself, the one bringing the offering.

phrases.english: so let it be an atonement;
and if not, let it be a gift offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִילְכָּךְ, אָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אליעזר's rule from step 1 to the practical case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second person brings an אשם תלוי on condition: atonement if he ate the חלב, a gift offering otherwise.

steps.title: רבי: an offering for each doubtful eating
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: someone ate possible חלב and was told about the doubt, then did the same thing again. רבי says that just as he would bring a חטאת for each one, he brings an אשם תלוי for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A person ate a piece that might be חלב and was told about it. Then he again ate a piece that might be חלב and was told about it. רבי says: Just as he brings a חטאת for each one, he brings an אשם תלוי for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. It asks how many אשם תלוי offerings are needed for two separate doubtful eatings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that he was told about the doubt between the two eatings. רבי compares this to a certain sin, where each separate act needs its own חטאת. So each doubtful act needs its own אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece that may or may not be forbidden fat
And it became known to him (here, he learned of the doubt)
Sin offering, brought for an unintentional sin that is known for certain

phrases.english: The Sages taught: He ate something that may be forbidden fat
and it became known to him,
phrases.notes: He found out that there was a doubt. He did not find out for sure that it was חלב.

phrases.english: then again something that may be forbidden fat, and it became known to him —
Rabbi says: I say,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: just as he brings a sin offering
for each and every one,
so too he brings a provisional guilt offering
for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אָכַל סְפֵק חֵלֶב וְנוֹדַע לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on how many אשם תלוי offerings are needed for several doubtful sins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, when a person learned of the doubt between eatings, he brings a separate אשם תלוי for each one, just as he would bring separate חטאות.

steps.title: Other Sages: only one offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון disagree. They say only one אשם תלוי is brought, based on the פסוק 'על שגגתו אשר שגג'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: He brings only one אשם תלוי, as it says: 'for his error which he erred.' Even for many errors, he owes only one.
steps.whatsHappening: Three תנאים disagree with רבי. They say the person brings only one אשם תלוי for all the doubtful eatings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They learn from the doubled wording 'שגגתו אשר שגג' that one offering covers many errors. In their view, being told about the doubt in between does not split the offerings for an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: His unintentional error
Many unintentional errors

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this argument with the rule for a חטאת. This argument is only about how many אשם תלוי offerings he brings for doubtful sins.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Elazar
and Rabbi Shimon say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מֵבִיא אֶלָּא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי אֶחָד,
phrases.english: He brings only one provisional guilt offering,
as it is said: "for his error which he erred" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:18

phrases.english: even for many errors
he is obligated in only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing view to רבי in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one אשם תלוי is brought for many doubtful sins, learned from 'על שגגתו אשר שגג'.

steps.title: רבי זירא: knowing of a doubt splits the sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says רבי's opinion teaches a general rule: knowing about a doubt between sins divides them into separate חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Here רבי taught that knowledge of a doubt divides the sins into separate sin offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא draws a general rule out of רבי's words in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said 'just as he brings a חטאת for each one.' That shows he holds the person would owe separate חטאות if he later learned he really sinned. So learning about a doubt between the acts works like learning about a sin: it splits them into separate offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowledge of a doubt, meaning learning that one may have sinned
Divide, split into separate units

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי (as רבי זירא explains), knowing about a doubt in between sins splits them into separate חטאות, just as knowing for sure would.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a general rule about when several unintentional sins need several חטאות rather than one.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Here Rabbi taught:
Knowledge of an uncertainty
divides into separate sin offerings.
phrases.notes: He means: if he later finds out the pieces really were חלב, he owes a separate חטאת for each eating.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from רבי's statement in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Knowledge of a doubt between sins divides them into separate חטאות.

steps.title: רבא reads רבי's ruling differently
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רבי זירא's inference. Knowing about a doubt does not split sins into separate חטאות. רבי only meant that it splits them into separate אשמות תלויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Knowing about a doubt does not split the acts into separate חטאות. Rather, this is what רבי is teaching: Just as definite knowledge between the acts would mean a חטאת for each one, so too knowledge of a doubt between them means an אשם תלוי for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with רבי זירא's general rule. He explains רבי's ruling in a narrower way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא learned from רבי that a ידיעת ספק divides sins even for חטאות. רבא says רבי's comparison only goes as far as the אשם תלוי. Only יְדִיעָה וַדַּאי splits sins into separate חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing that you might have sinned (a doubt)
Knowing for sure that you sinned
Divide the sins so each needs its own חטאת
A 'hanging' guilt offering brought for a sin you are unsure you did

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not argue with רבי's ruling itself. Both agree that a separate אשם תלוי is brought for each act. They only argue about what this means for the חטאת.

phrases.english: Rava says:
Knowledge of a doubt does not divide the acts into separate sin offerings,
rather, this is what it is teaching:
phrases.notes: 'It' means רבי's statement in the ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה לוֹ יְדִיעָה וַדַּאי
phrases.english: Just as, if he had definite knowledge

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא חַטָּאת עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת,
phrases.english: he brings a sin offering for each and every one,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אִם הָיְתָה לוֹ יְדִיעַת סָפֵק
phrases.english: so too, if he had knowledge of a doubt

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
phrases.english: he brings a provisional guilt offering for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֵין יְדִיעוֹת סָפֵק מְחַלְּקוֹת לְחַטָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי זירא's inference from רבי's ruling
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רבי זירא's inference about חטאות. רבי's ruling about אשמות תלויים stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי's comparison only teaches about the אשם תלוי. It does not show that a doubt divides for חטאות.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: if the acts would only need one חטאת, how can they need a separate אשם תלוי each?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Don't you agree that knowing about a doubt divides the acts into separate חטאות? If you think it does not divide them, and he brings only one חטאת, why does he bring an אשם תלוי for each one?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's reading. He says the number of אשמות תלויים cannot be more than the number of חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי stands in for the חטאת a person would owe if he found out for sure. So if both acts would need just one חטאת, they should need just one אשם תלוי. רבא's reading leaves them out of line with each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't you hold? (a challenging question)
If it enters your mind (if you think)
Why?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And you, do you not hold
that knowledge of a doubt divides the acts into separate sin offerings?
For if it enters your mind
that the knowledges do not divide into separate sin offerings,
and he brings only one sin offering,

phrases.aramaic: אַמַּאי מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?
phrases.english: why does he bring a provisional guilt offering for each and every one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּסְבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a ידיעת ספק divides for אשמות תלויים but not for חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The number of אשמות תלויים follows the number of חטאות. A split for one must mean a split for the other.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up אביי
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא: whatever is divided for חטאות is also divided for אשמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: The general rule is this: whatever is divided for חטאות is also divided for אשמות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a source for his challenge. A ברייתא says חטאות and אשמות תלויים follow the same counting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties the two offerings together. אביי reads it to mean they always match. Since רבי gives a separate אשם תלוי for each act, each act must also need its own חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter
Divided, counted as separate
Guilt offerings (here, אשמות תלויים)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: the general rule of the matter is:
whatever is divided for sin offerings
is divided for guilt offerings!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, כְּלָלוֹ שֶׁל דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind אביי's challenge
steps.raayaObject: That separate אשמות תלויים only come where there would be separate חטאות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: כל שחלוקין בחטאות חלוקין באשמות
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule ties the אשם תלוי to the חטאת. That is why the count of one decides the count of the other.

steps.title: רבא בר חנן challenges אביי with יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר חנן asks אביי: if a doubt divides sins, then יום הכפורים should divide them too. Then חלב eaten before and after יום הכפורים would need two חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר חנן said to אביי: According to you, a ידיעת ספק divides the acts into separate חטאות. If so, take someone who ate a כזית of חלב before יום הכפורים and a כזית after it. יום הכפורים stands in place of an אשם תלוי. Would he also bring two חטאות?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר חנן now attacks אביי's view. He shows that it seems to lead to a strange result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום הכפורים atones for doubtful sins, just like an אשם תלוי does. So if a doubt divides sins because of the אשם תלוי, then יום הכפורים should divide them too. The question hints that saying two חטאות here is hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then... (pushing an idea to its end)
An olive-size amount, the amount needed to be liable
The Day of Atonement
So too? (would you really say this?)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rava bar Chanan said to Abaye:
And according to you, who said
knowledge of a doubt divides the acts into separate sin offerings,
if so, then:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל כְּזַיִת חֵלֶב לִפְנֵי יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים
phrases.english: he ate an olive-size of forbidden fat before Yom Kippur
and an olive-size of forbidden fat after Yom Kippur,

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים בִּמְקוֹם אָשָׁם תָּלוּי קָאֵי
phrases.english: and Yom Kippur stands in place of a provisional guilt offering
would you say that here too he brings two sin offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי: וּלְדִידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the attack back on אביי's position
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that a ידיעת ספק divides the acts into separate חטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a doubt divides because of the אשם תלוי, then יום הכפורים, which does the same job, should divide too. That would mean two חטאות, which seems hard to accept.

steps.title: The punchline: it was all one lapse of awareness
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר חנן finishes his challenge. The two olive-sizes of חלב were eaten in one single העלם, so they should need only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he ate them in one single lapse of awareness!
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the challenge from step 9. A single lapse of awareness normally means only one חטאת, so a rule that requires two must be wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was no real knowledge of the sin between the two eatings, so nothing should split them. If יום הכפורים, which works like an אשם תלוי, does not split them, then knowing about a doubt should not split them either. That knocks down אביי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: One single lapse of awareness. All the acts happened while the person was still unaware of the sin.

phrases.english: But he ate them in one single lapse of awareness!
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the usual printed גמרא; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'one'.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד אַכְלִינּוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that knowing about a doubt splits sins into separate חטאות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יום הכפורים atones like an אשם תלוי but clearly does not split one lapse of awareness. So knowing about a doubt should not split it either.

steps.title: Maybe יום הכפורים only atones for doubts the person knew about
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that יום הכפורים may atone only for doubts the person knew about. In the חלב case he never knew, so יום הכפורים cannot be compared to knowing about a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Who tells us that יום הכפורים atones for something he did not know about? Maybe it only atones when he knew about it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself by showing that the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's point is that knowing is the thing that splits sins. If יום הכפורים atones only for doubts that were known, then in the חלב case nothing happened in between, because he never knew. That explains why there is only one חטאת there.

keyTerms.meaning: Atones
It becomes known to him
Perhaps

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And who will tell us
that Yom Kippur atones
for what was not known to him?
Perhaps only when it was known to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן לֵימָא לַן דְּיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים מְכַפַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 9 and 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום הכפורים atones just like a known doubt, so it should split sins the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: יום הכפורים may atone only for doubts the person knew about, so it is not like the unknown חלב case.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה says יום הכפורים atones even for unknown sins
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's answer. The משנה says יום הכפורים atones whether or not the person knew about the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: We learned in the משנה, 'whether he knew or did not know.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down אביי's answer with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says outright that יום הכפורים atones even for sins the person never knew about. So אביי cannot say it works only for known doubts, and the challenge from step 9 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether he became aware or did not become aware

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
We learned: 'whether he became aware or did not become aware.'
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שבועות 2b about what יום הכפורים atones for.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹדַע וְלֹא הוֹדַע תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that יום הכפורים atones only for known doubts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A משנה states clearly that יום הכפורים atones even for unknown sins.

steps.title: Second version: חלב eaten in the morning and afternoon of יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רבא בר חנן asks about חלב eaten twice on יום הכפורים itself, once in the morning and once in the afternoon. Would that need two חטאות?
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבא בר חנן said to אביי: What if a person ate an olive-size of חלב on the morning of יום הכפורים and another olive-size in the afternoon? Would he really need two חטאות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a second version of רבא בר חנן's challenge. This time both eatings happen during יום הכפורים itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום הכפורים atones like an אשם תלוי. If that kind of atonement splits sins, as אביי's view suggests, then the day's atonement between the morning and the afternoon should split the two eatings. But they happened in one lapse of awareness, so two חטאות sounds wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-size of forbidden fat
Morning
Afternoon

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question added on top of the earlier one. It is a different version of the same challenge, so the answers in steps 11 and 12 belong to the first version only.

phrases.english: Some say,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rava bar Ḥanan said to Abaye:
What if he ate an olive-size of forbidden fat
in the morning on Yom Kippur
and an olive-size of forbidden fat in the afternoon on Yom Kippur,
would he really be obligated to bring two sin offerings?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the challenge from steps 9 and 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that atonement or knowledge of a doubt splits sins.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The atonement of יום הכפורים during the day would split two eatings from one lapse of awareness into two חטאות. That result seems absurd.

steps.title: Maybe יום הכפורים atones only once, from the evening
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that perhaps יום הכפורים does not atone at every hour. Maybe the whole day atones as one unit, starting from the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Who tells us that יום הכפורים atones at every moment? Maybe the whole day atones from the evening!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries to show that nothing atones between the morning and the afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יום הכפורים atones only once, at the start of the day, then no new atonement happens between the two eatings. So there is nothing to split them, and only one חטאת is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: At every hour, at every moment
From the evening, when the day begins

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And who will tell us
that Yom Kippur atones at every hour?
Perhaps the whole day atones from the evening!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן לֵימָא לַן דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים כֹּל שַׁעְתָּא מְכַפַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום הכפורים atones all through the day, so it would separate a morning sin from an afternoon sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe the whole day atones as one unit from the evening, so nothing separates the two eatings.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: even at nightfall the day still atones
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה rejects אביי's answer with a ברייתא. A doubtful sin that comes up on יום הכפורים, even right at nightfall, is exempt, because the whole day atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said to him: Fool! It is taught: If a doubtful sin came his way on יום הכפורים, even at nightfall, he is exempt, because the whole day atones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה sharply rejects אביי's suggestion using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sin at nightfall happens after the evening start of the day, yet the day still atones for it. So יום הכפורים keeps atoning all day long, and it would atone between the morning and the afternoon. אביי's answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Fool; literally 'beet,' a sharp word of rebuke
A doubtful sin, where he is not sure whether he sinned
At nightfall, at the very end of the day
Exempt, here meaning exempt from an אשם תלוי

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said to him:
Fool! It is taught:
One who encountered a doubtful sin
on Yom Kippur, even at nightfall,
is exempt, because the entire day atones!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרָדָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's answer in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that יום הכפורים atones only once, from the evening.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ברייתא shows the day atones even for a sin at nightfall, so it atones all day long.
steps.whyThisMatters: This establishes that the atonement of יום הכפורים covers every moment of the day. That is exactly what the next challenge builds on.

steps.title: Eating and drinking on יום הכפורים need only one חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין challenges אביי from a משנה. Someone who ate and drank on יום הכפורים in one lapse of awareness brings only one חטאת, even though the day atoned between the two acts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין objected: 'If he ate and drank in one lapse of awareness, he brings only one חטאת.' But between the eating and the drinking there must have been some time in the day. In that time the doubt could have become known to him and the day would have atoned, since יום הכפורים takes the place of an אשם תלוי. Yet the משנה says he brings only one חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge against אביי, this time from a משנה about sinning on יום הכפורים itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that יום הכפורים atones all day and works like an אשם תלוי. So between the eating and the drinking, the day's atonement should split the two acts into two חטאות according to אביי. The משנה says only one, which contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: A stretch of time
A guilt offering brought for a doubtful sin, which protects him until he finds out
Stands in place of

steps.whatToRemember: Two facts are now set: יום הכפורים atones for unknown doubts, and it atones all day long. Together they make the eating-and-drinking משנה a strong challenge to אביי's rule that atonement or knowledge of a doubt splits sins.

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin raised an objection:
If he ate and drank in one lapse of awareness,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in יומא 81a about someone who forgot it was יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: he is liable to bring only one sin offering.
But between eating and drinking

phrases.aramaic: אִי אֶפְשָׁר דְּלֹא הֲוָה שְׁהוּת בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: it is impossible that there was no stretch of time during the day,
in which it could become known to him and atone for him,

phrases.aramaic: דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים בִּמְקוֹם אָשָׁם תָּלוּי קָאֵי,
phrases.english: since Yom Kippur stands in place of a provisional guilt offering,
and yet it teaches: 'He is liable to bring only one sin offering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 15's point that יום הכפורים atones all day, and uses it to challenge אביי from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that atonement or knowledge of a doubt splits sins into separate חטאות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The day's atonement between the eating and the drinking should split them into two חטאות. Yet the משנה requires only one.

steps.title: Finishing the challenge: he should owe two חטאות
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין completes his challenge. If awareness of a doubtful sin divides sins, then the person who ate and drank on יום הכפורים should owe two חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that awareness of a doubtful sin divides sins into separate חטאות, then he should be obligated to bring two חטאות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question begun in the last step. It spells out the problem: the rule being discussed would give this person two חטאות, but the משנה says he brings one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day of יום הכפורים atoned in between the eating and the drinking. If something like awareness of a doubtful sin is enough to split two sins, that atonement in the middle should split them too. But the משנה says only one חטאת, so the rule seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would think. It introduces an idea the גמרא is about to show leads to a problem.
Moments of awareness that one may have sinned, without knowing for sure.
They divide the sins, so that each one needs its own חטאת.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that awareness of uncertainty divides into separate sin offerings,
then he should be liable to two sin offerings!
phrases.notes: This is the person in the משנה who ate and then drank on יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ יְדִיעוֹת סָפֵק מְחַלְּקוֹת לְחַטָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא of רב אידי בר אבין that began in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that awareness of a doubtful sin, or the day's atonement, splits sins into separate חטאות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were true, the atonement of the day between eating and drinking should create two חטאות. The משנה rules there is only one.

steps.title: רבי זירא's rule follows רבי, and the משנה follows רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי זירא spoke according to רבי's view. The משנה about eating and drinking follows רבנן, who disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: when רבי זירא said this, it was according to רבי. This משנה follows רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by putting the two sources under two different opinions. רבי זירא's rule belongs to רבי, and the משנה belongs to רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction disappears once each source follows a different תנא. The משנה's ruling of one חטאת shows only what רבנן hold. It does not disprove a rule stated according to רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with רבי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא – לְרַבִּי,
phrases.english: They say: when Rabbi Zeira said it, it was according to Rabbi;
phrases.notes: "רבי" alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: this one is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the משנה about eating and drinking on יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא – לְרַבִּי, הָא – רַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from steps 16 and 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים (רבי and רבנן).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to contradict רבי זירא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי זירא's rule follows רבי, and the משנה follows רבנן, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: The end of the משנה follows רבי, so the beginning should too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. The end of that same משנה implies that someone who drinks vinegar on יום הכפורים is liable, and that is רבי's view. So the beginning of the משנה should also follow רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the משנה is רבי, since it teaches: if he drank fish liquid or fish brine, he is exempt. That means if he drank vinegar, he is liable. And who holds that? רבי, as a ברייתא teaches: vinegar does not revive the spirit. רבי says: I say vinegar does revive the spirit. And since the end of the משנה is רבי, the beginning should also be רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. It proves that the end of the משנה follows רבי, so it seems the beginning must follow רבי as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts someone who drinks fish liquid or brine, which hints that vinegar would make him liable. A ברייתא shows that only רבי treats vinegar as a real drink that "revives the spirit." Normally one משנה follows one תנא from start to finish, so the eating-and-drinking clause at the beginning should also be רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא.
The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא.
The salty liquid from pickled fish, and fish brine.
Vinegar.
Revives the spirit, meaning it truly refreshes like a real drink.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two parts of the משנה. The רישא, the beginning, is about eating and drinking in one lapse, which gives only one חטאת. The סיפא, the end, is about which liquids count as drinking. The argument here is about the beginning, but the proof comes from the end.

phrases.english: But from the latter clause, it is Rabbi,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: שָׁתָה צִיר אוֹ מוּרְיָיס – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: as it teaches: if he drank fish liquid or brine, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה about יום הכפורים (יומא פא.).

phrases.english: This implies that for vinegar, he is liable,
And who is it? It is Rabbi,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: חוֹמֶץ אֵין מֵשִׁיב אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ,
phrases.english: as it is taught: vinegar does not revive the spirit,
Rabbi says: I say,
vinegar does revive the spirit.
And since the latter clause is Rabbi, the first clause is also Rabbi!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18, which said the משנה follows רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the eating-and-drinking clause of the משנה follows רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vinegar inference in the סיפא matches only רבי's view. A single משנה is normally taken to follow one תנא throughout, so the רישא should be רבי too, and the contradiction with רבי זירא comes back.

steps.title: The end follows רבי and the beginning follows רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one משנה can be split: the end follows רבי, and the beginning follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: the end is רבי, and the beginning is רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its earlier answer. It says the משנה does not have to follow one opinion all the way through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we assume a משנה follows a single תנא, but here the גמרא accepts a split. The vinegar part follows רבי, and the eating-and-drinking part follows רבנן. That keeps רבי זירא's rule safe as רבי's view.

phrases.english: They say: the latter clause is Rabbi; the first clause is the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: סֵיפָא – רַבִּי, רֵישָׁא – רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 and defends the answer of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one משנה between two תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the end of the משנה is רבי, the beginning must be רבי too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The end follows רבי and the beginning follows רבנן, so the beginning does not contradict רבי זירא's rule according to רבי.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge from eating and drinking on יום הכפורים is answered by assigning sources to different views. רבי זירא's rule follows רבי. The משנה's first clause follows רבנן, even though its last clause follows רבי.

steps.title: Benefits on different days, even years apart, still combine
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a new challenge from a ברייתא. Eating or benefiting from holy property on one day and again on another, even three years apart, can combine into one total. The ברייתא asks where this is learned from.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged him: if he ate today and ate tomorrow, benefited today and benefited tomorrow, ate today and benefited tomorrow, or benefited today and ate tomorrow, even from now until three years later, how do we know that they combine with each other?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a new challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up his question; the rest of the ברייתא and his point come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists every mix of eating and benefiting on two different days. It says they still join together, even with years in between. רבא's point, made in the next step, is that a gap of years means a יום הכפורים must have come in between, and according to אביי that atonement should have split the acts.

keyTerms.meaning: He benefited, meaning he used the item for his own benefit.
They combine, adding up to one amount.
From where do we know? It asks for the source.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" here is אביי, whose answer is being challenged.

phrases.english: If he ate today and ate tomorrow,
phrases.notes: This is about holy property, where you need a פרוטה's worth to owe an אשם.

phrases.english: benefited today and benefited tomorrow,
ate today and benefited tomorrow,
benefited today and ate tomorrow,
and even from now until three years,

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁהֵן מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה?
phrases.english: from where do we know that they combine with each other?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge against אביי, after the challenge of steps 16–20 was resolved.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that knowledge of a doubt, and likewise יום הכפורים, which stands in place of an אשם תלוי, splits acts into separate units.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up here: the ברייתא says acts years apart still combine. רבא will use this to argue against אביי once the ברייתא is finished.

steps.title: The פסוק includes adding up, but didn't יום הכפורים already atone?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from "תמעול מעל" that pieces of מעילה combine across time. רבא asks how this can be, since יום הכפורים should have atoned for the first piece and cut it off from the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "תמעול מעל" (commits a misuse), and this doubled wording includes adding up separate small amounts. But why should they add up? יום הכפורים already atoned for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its source from the פסוק. Then רבא finishes his challenge: יום הכפורים passed between the two acts, so it should separate them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the acts were years apart, at least one יום הכפורים came between them. יום הכפורים atones for doubtful sins, much as an אשם תלוי does. So under the view that awareness of a doubt divides sins, יום הכפורים should also divide them, and the two halves should not combine.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches": introduces the פסוק used as a source
"Commits a misuse": doubled wording in the פסוק about מעילה
"It included": the extra wording adds a case to the law
יום הכפורים atoned: the day brings atonement

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the פסוק itself. רבא accepts the ברייתא. He is using it to attack the view that atonement or awareness splits sins apart.

phrases.english: The verse states: "commits a misuse" — it included.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:15. The doubled verb is read as including small amounts that add up over time.

phrases.english: But why?
Yom Kippur already atoned for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי, הָא כַּיפַּר עֲלֵיהּ יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's challenge that began in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that awareness of a doubtful sin (and likewise יום הכפורים) divides sins into separate units
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Acts of מעילה years apart combine according to the ברייתא, even though a יום הכפורים passed in between. So atonement does not split them.

steps.title: יום הכפורים atones for the prohibition, not for money owed
steps.stepSummary: יום הכפורים atones only for the איסור. It does not erase a money obligation. מעילה involves money, so the amounts still combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: When does יום הכפורים atone? For a prohibition. It does not atone for a money matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא. יום הכפורים clears the sin side of an act, but it does not cancel money that is owed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעילה creates a debt to הקדש. Since יום הכפורים does not wipe out that debt, it cannot split the money owed into two parts. The amounts add up to a פרוטה, and he must bring an אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: A ritual prohibition
Money, a financial obligation

phrases.english: They say: When does Yom Kippur atone?
For a prohibition.
For money it does not atone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: כִּי מְכַפַּר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of יום הכפורים's atonement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום הכפורים atoned for the first act and cut it off from the second
steps.terutzMaskana: Atonement does not touch the money obligation of מעילה, so the amounts still combine

steps.title: יום הכפורים does not atone for half a measure
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: יום הכפורים atones only for a full שיעור. Less than a פרוטה of מעילה is not atoned, so it stays and combines with the later piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say this: When does יום הכפורים atone? For a full measure. For half a measure it does not atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer to רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first act was less than a פרוטה, so it was not yet a full sin. יום הכפורים did nothing to it. Nothing was split, and the two halves join to make a full שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: "If you want, say": introduces another answer
The required minimum amount
Half of the required amount

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
When does Yom Kippur atone?
For the entire measure.
For half a measure it does not atone.
phrases.notes: Here the measure is a פרוטה's worth of הקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כִּי מְכַפַּר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting atonement to a full שיעור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יום הכפורים atoned for the first half and separated it
steps.terutzMaskana: Less than a full שיעור is not atoned, so it remains and combines

steps.title: ריש לקיש: רבי taught that doubtful awareness divides
steps.stepSummary: Agreeing with רבי זירא, ריש לקיש says that in the ברייתא רבי taught that ידיעות ספק divide sins into separate חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said ריש לקיש: Here רבי taught that awareness of doubt divides sins into separate חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings other אמוראים on the main question. ריש לקיש takes the same side as רבי זירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time a person becomes aware that he may have sinned, that awareness closes off a unit. Later sins then need their own חטאת. ריש לקיש reads this rule into רבי's words in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness of a doubtful sin, knowing you may have sinned
They divide into separate units
Sin offerings

phrases.english: And so said Reish Lakish:
phrases.notes: "And so" means he agrees with רבי זירא from earlier.

phrases.english: Here Rebbi taught:
Awareness of doubt divides for sin offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section with other אמוראים' views on the main question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, ידיעות ספק divide sins into separate חטאות

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Doubtful awareness does not divide
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees. ידיעות ספק do not divide sins into separate חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Awareness of doubt does not divide sins into separate חטאות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite view, siding with רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, only certain knowledge of a sin closes off a unit. Doubtful awareness does not. So all the sins before he learns for sure need just one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not divide

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש (like רבי זירא): ידיעות ספק divide. רבי יוחנן (like רבא): they do not divide.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Awareness of doubt does not divide for sin offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵין יְדִיעוֹת סָפֵק מְחַלְּקוֹת לְחַטָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing side of ריש לקיש's statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ידיעות ספק do not divide sins into separate חטאות

steps.title: How רבי יוחנן reads the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the ברייתא only means that knowledge of a doubt requires a separate אשם תלוי for each piece. It does not mean separate חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the ברייתא means: if he would bring a חטאת for each piece when he had clear knowledge, then he brings an אשם תלוי for each piece when he had knowledge of a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן continues his statement and explains how he reads רבי's words in the ברייתא, so that they fit his view that ידיעות ספק do not divide חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש read the ברייתא as saying that knowing about a doubt splits the sins into separate חטאות. רבי יוחנן says the ברייתא is only comparing two offerings. Clear knowledge splits sins for חטאת, and knowledge of a doubt splits them only for אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Clear, certain knowledge that he sinned
Knowing that he might have sinned
Provisional guilt offering, brought when one is not sure he sinned
For each and every one, meaning a separate offering for each act

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying knowledge of a doubt creates separate חטאות. According to רבי יוחנן it only creates separate אשמות תלויים.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it teaches:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's way of reading the ברייתא of רבי from the earlier steps.

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה לוֹ יְדִיעָה וַדַּאי
phrases.english: Just as, if he had definite knowledge,
he brings an offering for each and every one,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אִם הָיְתָה לוֹ יְדִיעַת סָפֵק
phrases.english: so too, if he had knowledge of a doubt,

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
phrases.english: he brings a provisional guilt offering for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יוחנן (step 26) handles the ברייתא that ריש לקיש cited (step 25).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to say that ידיעות ספק divide sins into separate חטאות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only says that ידיעות ספק divide sins for אשם תלוי, the way clear knowledge divides them for חטאת.

steps.title: The ברייתא's wording fits רבי יוחנן but not ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא hangs the rule of the אשם on the rule of the חטאת. That fits רבי יוחנן. According to ריש לקיש, it should have hung the חטאת on the אשם. The גמרא leaves this unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יוחנן this is fine, because the ברייתא makes the אשם depend on the חטאת. But for ריש לקיש, it should have made the חטאת depend on the אשם! This is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from the way the ברייתא is worded and ends with "קשיא": the question stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says, in effect, "just as with חטאת, so too with אשם." That matches רבי יוחנן, who learns the אשם rule from the known חטאת rule. If ריש לקיש were right that knowledge of a doubt is what divides חטאות, the ברייתא should have taught the חטאת rule from the אשם rule instead.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well, it makes sense (according to one view)
Hangs, makes one thing depend on another
He should have (said it this way)
It is difficult: a question left unanswered, though the view is not rejected

phrases.english: It works well according to Rabbi Yochanan:
that is why it makes the guilt offering depend on the sin offering.
But according to Reish Lakish,
it should have made the sin offering depend on the guilt offering!
It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַיְינוּ דְּקָא תָלֵי לְאָשָׁם בְּחַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יוחנן's reading from step 27 to show that the ברייתא's wording is hard for ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading of the ברייתא (step 25)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא learns the אשם from the חטאת. That fits רבי יוחנן. If ריש לקיש were right, the order should be reversed.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's wording supports רבי יוחנן. The גמרא leaves this as a קשיא against ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Announcing a contradiction within each sage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that it will show רבי יוחנן contradicting himself and ריש לקיש contradicting himself, based on a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא sets one statement of רבי יוחנן against another of his, and one statement of ריש לקיש against another of his.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is preparing a new challenge: each sage seems to hold the opposite view somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagreed about whether ידיעות ספק divide sins. The גמרא now says that, in another case, each of them seems to take the other's position. The ברייתא that comes next sets up that case.

keyTerms.meaning: And he set against: points out a contradiction between two statements

phrases.english: And he set a statement of Rabbi Yochanan against a statement of Rabbi Yochanan,
and set a statement of Reish Lakish against a statement of Reish Lakish,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָמֵי דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wording issue and opens a new challenge: inner contradictions in both sages.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each sage's view on ידיעות ספק will be shown to clash with his own statement elsewhere.

steps.title: The ברייתא of the two paths
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes two paths, one impure and one pure, without knowing which is which. It rules on a person who walked on them and entered the מקדש in different orders.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two paths, one impure and one pure. If he walked on the first and did not enter, then walked on the second and entered, he is liable. If he walked on the first and entered, he is exempt; if he then walked on the second and entered, he is liable. If he walked on the first and entered, then was sprinkled twice and immersed, and then walked on the second and entered, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that will be the basis for the contradictions it just announced. This step is the source; the challenge itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After walking both paths he is surely impure, so entering after that makes him liable. After only one path, he is just a doubt, so one entry alone makes him exempt. Once he has entered after each path, one of the two entries was surely impure, so he is liable, even if he purified himself in between.

keyTerms.meaning: Paths
Ritually impure
Ritually pure
Liable, must bring an offering
Exempt, does not bring an offering
Was sprinkled, sprinkled again, and immersed: the steps of purifying from corpse impurity

steps.whyThisMatters: The middle and last cases involve two doubtful acts that only together add up to a sure sin. That is exactly where the question of what separates sins will matter for each sage.

phrases.english: As it is taught: two paths,
one impure and one pure,
and he walked on the first and did not enter,
phrases.notes: Enter means going into the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: then on the second and entered: he is liable.
If he walked on the first and entered: he is exempt,
then on the second and entered: he is liable.
If he walked on the first and entered,
and was sprinkled, and sprinkled again, and immersed,
phrases.notes: These are the sprinklings of the ashes of the פרה אדומה, then immersing in a מקוה.

phrases.english: and walked on the second and entered: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא שְׁנֵי שְׁבִילִין אֶחָד טָמֵא וְאֶחָד טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that step 29 said would show contradictions in both sages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Walking both paths and then entering makes him liable. One doubtful entry alone makes him exempt. Entering after each path makes him liable, even if he purified himself between the two entries.
